title: SAP Sales Order Cross-Application Integration Map

meta.summary: Normalizes sales-order origins, cross-application execution handoffs and business events without turning every system topology into a new sales process.

attribution.preferred_citation: Dzmitryi Kharlanau. "SAP Sales Order Cross-Application Integration Map". CC BY-NC 4.0. https://dkharlanau.github.io/labs/enterprise-context/sales-processes/integrations/

code_contract.rule: Origin answers who creates or orchestrates the order. Process answers which business contract runs. Handoff answers which application owns the next execution decision.

origins.title: External App via A2X API
origins.key_decision: Keep S/4HANA semantics authoritative for order behavior unless ownership is explicitly delegated.

origins.title: External Web Shop / Landscape via A2A Bulk
origins.key_decision: Treat technical receipt and business creation as different statuses.

origins.title: External Buyer / EDI-style B2B
origins.key_decision: Model the full buyer-supplier document conversation, not only inbound order creation.

origins.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Order Management
origins.key_decision: Decide which synchronous answers Commerce needs from S/4HANA: price, ATP, credit, simulation.

origins.title: SAP CPQ Quote to Sales Order
origins.key_decision: Preserve quote-to-order trace and pricing/configuration parity.

origins.title: SAP Sales Cloud v2 Opportunity-to-Order
origins.key_decision: CRM owns pipeline/engagement; ERP owns the executable sales contract and fulfillment.

origins.title: Solution Order Orchestration
origins.key_decision: A solution item can distribute into different business objects; failure must name the failed follow-up owner.

origins.title: Subscription Delivery Plan to Sales Order
origins.key_decision: Contract lifecycle remains outside the generated order.

origins.title: Customer Project to Sales Order Context
origins.key_decision: Project stage and billing model govern which sales operations are valid.

handoffs.via: requirements, planned order, production order or assembly object
handoffs.owns_next: components, production execution and feasible manufacturing dates
project structure, project stock/service execution and costs
supplier sourcing, confirmations, receipt and invoice evidence
warehouse tasks, picking, packing, receiving and warehouse inspection

handoffs.via: sales order/scheduling agreement and delivery integration
handoffs.owns_next: transport planning, execution and freight settlement

handoffs.via: legal control, embargo and screening status
credit check and documented credit decision

handoffs.owns_next: receivable, revenue, COGS, margin and recognition

handoffs.trigger: service, repair, subscription or mixed solution scope

events.pattern: publish event, route through event infrastructure, fetch richer detail by API when required
avoid_for: a synchronous promise calculation that must finish before the customer sees confirmation

lead_prompts: Is this a new business process or only a new order origin?
Which system owns price, ATP, credit and configuration at the customer-promise moment?
Which application owns the next irreversible decision?
Which cross-system key proves end-to-end correlation?
Which calls must be synchronous and which should be event/message driven?
